unreg:all_star_weekend_events.label: NBA All-Star Weekend skills contests (3-point, slam dunk, Shooting Stars)
unreg:all_star_weekend_events.target: Winner of an All-Star Weekend skills contest: the 3-Point Contest, the Slam Dunk Contest or the Shooting Stars team contest
unreg:all_star_weekend_events.mechanism: Each series settles on the winner of a one-off skills contest: the league invites the field and a withdrawn named player resolves No (3PT, dunk); performance is timed rack shooting with no defender, judged dunks with a miss risk, or a three-player team (two current players and a legend) shooting from seven fixed spots against a 70-second clock; the format turns performance into a winner through rounds, advancement cuts, a final that resets scores and tie procedures. Winners are maxima over a few noisy scores, so favourites are capped and format parameters matter as much as skill. Inputs are scoped per series because the three processes are disjoint.

attach.why: Format parameters of the skills contests (scoring scale, rounds, advancement, ties, shoot-offs) define what a win means in the 3PT, dunk and Shooting Stars series, each field with a provenance flag.
Injury reports before the weekend drive withdrawals and replacement entrants in the 3PT and dunk fields and roster changes for Shooting Stars teams.
Announcements on contest fields, team rosters, format and participation arrive as news before official lists (KXNBA3PTCONTEST, KXNBASLAMDUNK, KXNBASHOOTINGSTARS).
Format changes announced by the league (ball values, locations, rounds, team composition) alter the scoring rules of the skills contests.
Announcement timing of contest fields, team rosters and format sets the as-of date for every skills-contest input.
Rules fix withdrawal-to-No for the 3PT and dunk series, the 70 s 3PT round and advancement, the dunk round structure, and expose the empty text of KXNBASHOOTINGSTARS.
Official contest-winner announcements are the labels and need reconciling with the contract source.

Applies to KXNBASHOOTINGSTARS only: four of the seven Shooting Stars locations are 2-point locations (official 2026 rules PDF) that the 3-point-only spot profile cannot estimate, so team skill needs rim, baseline, elbow and top-of-key conversion and tempo.
Team strength of the actual All-Star rosters (nationality-built in 2026; the 2025 construction is UNVERIFIED) in a low-defence exhibition is the core input of every exhibition series.
Rising Stars (quoted 40/25 targets, KXNBARISINGSTARS) is a race, so its winner requires this model; any 2025 All-Star race format is UNVERIFIED and not assumed, and a clock rule is unstated.
Rising Stars teams (KXNBARISINGSTARS only) of first/second-year and G League players need their own shrunk, cross-league strength rating.
The 2026 nationality split (KXNBAALLSTARGAME only; at least 16 US and 8 international players, Commissioner additions) decides how deep the World team is against the two US teams.
Three-point volume shapes roster scoring in a high-3PA exhibition; context for the 2026 All-Star Game rosters only.

unreg:all_star_exhibition_games.target: Which team wins an All-Star Weekend exhibition game or mini-tournament (the All-Star Game and the Rising Stars tournament) under the event's own format.
unreg:all_star_exhibition_games.mechanism: An All-Star exhibition champion comes from selected or drafted rosters (a nationality split with Commissioner additions in 2026, coach drafts for Rising Stars), the minutes and effort of the players who appear in games of only 12 minutes or races to 40 and 25, a single-game conversion with large variance, and a tournament structure (Game-1-dependent pairings, point-differential tiebreak, seeding to a final) that turns single games into a champion. Inputs are scoped per series (KXNBAALLSTARGAME: nationality quota, roster composite, path simulation; KXNBARISINGSTARS: Rising Stars rating and race model; KXNBAALLSTAR: roster composite and path simulation only, its 2025 format being UNVERIFIED) because the formats differ.

attach.why: The MVP rule resolves a non-participating named player to No, so the probability that an All-Star selectee does not play (not contest-field withdrawal) multiplies every Yes price.
Regular-season production is only a context prior for an exhibition MVP; its odds and media-consensus narrative proxies are market-derived and are not used.
Offensive impact is context for team strength through the roster composite; it does not drive the exhibition MVP vote.
